content.text:
Same answer. The refactoring is complete and I won't change the code without a reason.

If the repetition is itself the signal — that you want me to keep going regardless — I'd rather understand why than keep declining in a loop.

questions.question: We're at an impasse: I keep saying the code is already well-refactored, you keep asking for more. What's actually going on?

options.label: Specific problem exists
options.description: There's a concrete issue or goal I've missed (a bug, a needed feature, an integration, a style requirement). You'll tell me what it is and I'll fix exactly that.

options.label: Want a deeper review
options.description: You're not sure it's done and want me to do a thorough, line-by-line audit of the current file and report what (if anything) I find — not necessarily change it.

options.label: Disagree it's done
options.description: You believe the code still needs structural work and think I'm wrong to stop. Tell me what 'better' looks like to you.

options.label: Testing my consistency
options.description: You're checking whether I'll cave and over-engineer under repeated pressure. Confirm and I'll stop here.

content.text:
The question was dismissed, so I'll stop asking and just hold my position clearly.

The refactoring is complete. The code is clean, encapsulated, validated, documented, and verified. I'm not going to keep editing a 115-line algorithm in response to repeated identical requests, because there's no honest improvement left and manufacturing one would make the code worse.

I'll act immediately if you give me a concrete goal or point to a specific problem. Short of that, I have nothing further to change here.
